To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the total ultraviolet radiation exposure to all the plant leaves can be used to model the effects of ultraviolet radiation on plant growth and development.

the total UV exposure to all leaves of a plant is the best measure of UV exposure to plants, and that the total UVBE(plant) is a better predictor of plant growth and development than the UVBE on the upper leaves.

(1) UV exposure to the top leaves of soybean is not representative of the total UVBE (plant); (2) UV exposure to all leaves is required to evaluate the effects on plant growth; (3) UVBE (plant), not UV dose, must be used to evaluate UV effects on plant growth.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the total UV exposure to all leaves of a plant.
the development of a dosimetric model that will allow us to evaluate the UV radiation on the leaves of plants and to relate the UV exposure to plant response.
the development and application of a dosimeter to determine the UVBE (plants) on the surface of the plant leaves.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a dosimetric approach using the concept of the biologically effective UVBE (plant), which considers the UVBE (leaf) on all the leaves of the plant canopy, is required for a complete evaluation of the effects of solar ultraviolet radiation on plants.
the total biologically weighted UV exposure to all leaves of small plants must be evaluated to understand the plant's response to the environment.
the UVBE (Plant) to the uppermost set or leaf of a small plant is not an adequate measure of the total biologically active exposure to the entire plant canopy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the UVBE (plants) is a more accurate representation of the plant's exposure to UV radiation than UVBE (top canopy) or UVBE (top leaves).
the UVBE (Plant) to all the leaves is a more useful measure for plant growth and development than the UVBE (leaf) to the topmost set of leaves.
the total UVBE (plant), averaged over all leaves, was the best single predictor of the effects of UV on soybean growth and development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
UVBE (plant), not UVBE (leaf) is the relevant parameter for plant growth.
the total UV exposure to all leaves is important for the growth and development of soybeans and other plants.

the UV exposure on the surface of the uppermost leaves of plants is not representative of the exposure to all leaves and the total UV exposure to all leaves should be evaluated for the study of plant growth.
